{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/trial.csv')

# Step 1: Deduplicate by patient_id, keeping the row with the highest sample_seq
# First, ensure we only keep one row per patient
# Sort by patient_id and sample_seq (descending) to prioritize higher sample_seq
df_dedup = df.sort_values(by=['patient_id', 'sample_seq'], ascending=[True, False])

# Drop duplicates on patient_id, keeping the first (i.e., highest sample_seq)
df_dedup = df_dedup.drop_duplicates(subset=['patient_id'], keep='first')

# Now check: how many rows?
print(f'Number of rows after deduplication: {len(df_dedup)}')

# Check that we have 800 unique patients (848 total - 48 duplicates)
print(f'Number of unique patients: {df_dedup["patient_id"].nunique()}')

# Verify that the deduplication worked: no more duplicates
print(f'Any duplicate patient_id after deduplication? {df_dedup["patient_id"].duplicated().any()}')"}
